milestones.title: Transfer the existing nine-point endpoint configuration proof
milestones.milestone_description: Transfer the authenticated Lean construction of the boundary triangle, its three cap regions, and its distinguished vertices for any nine-point counterexample. This is an existing source proof, not a request to reconstruct the geometry. It is the first supporting result in the nine-point argument.

milestones.title: Exclude the interior-point/opposite-vertex pattern at the first triangle vertex
milestones.milestone_description: For the first distinguished triangle vertex, rule out an escaping four-point distance class containing one point in the second cap interior and the second triangle vertex in the third cap. The repository already contains the source proof, and this milestone records its verified transfer.

milestones.title: Exclude the interior-point/opposite-vertex pattern at the second triangle vertex
milestones.milestone_description: At the second distinguished triangle vertex, rule out the cyclic relabelling of the interior-point/opposite-vertex witness pattern excluded at the first vertex. The proof transports the already verified first-vertex result around the boundary triangle.

milestones.title: Exclude the two-interior-point pattern at the first triangle vertex
milestones.milestone_description: For the first distinguished triangle vertex, rule out an escaping four-point distance class containing one point in each of the other two cap interiors. The proof uses the verified second-vertex interior-point/opposite-vertex exclusion.

milestones.title: Exclude the opposite-vertex/interior-point pattern at the first triangle vertex
milestones.milestone_description: For the first distinguished triangle vertex, rule out an escaping four-point distance class containing the third triangle vertex in the second cap and one point in the third cap interior. The repository already contains the source proof, and this milestone records its verified transfer.

milestones.title: Exclude the remaining cyclic witness-location patterns
milestones.milestone_description: Use cyclic relabelling of the boundary triangle to exclude the five remaining versions of the two-interior-point, interior-point/opposite-vertex, and opposite-vertex/interior-point patterns at the second and third distinguished vertices.

milestones.title: Prove cap containment for four-point distance classes
milestones.milestone_description: After all nine escaped witness-location patterns have been excluded, prove that every positive-radius distance class with at least four points centered at a distinguished triangle vertex lies entirely in the corresponding cap region.

milestones.title: Problem 97 supporting lemma: overlap among four two-point supports
milestones.milestone_description: Let U be a finite set with at most seven elements, and let A, B, C, D be two-element subsets of U. Suppose A and B are disjoint, A and C are disjoint, and C and D are disjoint. Then at least one of A ∩ D, B ∩ C, or B ∩ D is nonempty. This counting lemma replaces enumeration inside a sixteen-case support analysis; the geometric exclusions and the removable-vertex conclusion remain separate obligations.

milestones.title: Alternative resolution — construct a Problem 97 counterexample
milestones.milestone_description: Construct a nonempty finite set in strictly convex position in the Euclidean plane for which every vertex has at least four other points at one positive distance, possibly a different distance at each vertex. This is the counterexample branch for Problem 97. A proof refutes Problem 97 and should also be submitted as a disproof of the mission's combined affirmative theorem.

milestones.title: Place all three cap regions on equal-radius circles
milestones.milestone_description: After cap containment is established, prove that one positive radius places every point of each endpoint cap on the circle centered at its corresponding distinguished triangle vertex. The repository already contains the source proof, and this milestone records its verified transfer.

milestones.title: Exclude a four-witness point from every cap interior
milestones.milestone_description: Assuming cap containment and the four-equidistant-points property, prove that no point of the nine-point configuration lies in the interior of any endpoint cap. This exhausts the final geometric case and completes the exact nine-point exclusion.

milestones.title: Descent: a minimal counterexample with more than nine vertices has a removable vertex
milestones.milestone_description: Let A be a nonempty finite set in strictly convex position with more than nine vertices and with four equidistant witnesses at every vertex. Assume every smaller nonempty set with the same two properties is contradictory. Prove that some vertex can be deleted while preserving the four-witness property; convex independence and the strict decrease in cardinality then contradict minimality. This is the remaining large-cardinality step. The source formalization still has one unresolved geometric case and another case relying on compiled finite certificates, so it is not yet ready for platform verification. Dumitrescu attribution applies to the separate counting route.

milestones.title: Transfer the existing exact-ten exclusion proof
milestones.milestone_description: Transfer the repository's existing proof that a ten-point set in strictly convex position cannot have four equidistant witnesses at every vertex. Reuse the published exact nine-point result as a dependency. The source proof currently uses compiled finite-certificate verification, so the transfer must satisfy and clearly report the platform's trust policy.

milestones.title: Transfer the existing exact-eleven exclusion proof
milestones.milestone_description: After the exact ten-point transfer, transfer the repository's existing proof that an eleven-point set in strictly convex position cannot have four equidistant witnesses at every vertex. The source proof currently uses compiled finite-certificate verification, so the transfer must satisfy and clearly report the platform's trust policy.

theorems.natural_language_statement: Public names connecting the finite-nine endpoint geometry to the accepted counting definitions.

Cap containment and indexed cap interiors used in the final exact nine-point contradiction.
Public data types recording escaped four-point witness patterns, together with the geometric facts supplied by the first cap-containment case analysis.
A public record of eight geometric contradictions for the interior-point/opposite-vertex witness pattern when each cap interior contains exactly two points.
Every nine-point endpoint configuration supplies the two-point cap-layout and geometric facts needed to exclude the remaining escaped witness-location patterns.
For every nine-point endpoint configuration in which each cap interior contains exactly two points, eight geometric contradictions rule out the interior-point/opposite-vertex witness pattern.
Every nine-point convex counterexample with four equidistant witnesses at each vertex determines a boundary triangle and three associated cap regions used in the subsequent case analysis.
At the first distinguished triangle vertex, an escaping four-point distance class cannot contain one point in the second cap interior together with the second triangle vertex in the third cap.
At the second distinguished triangle vertex, the cyclic relabelling of the interior-point/opposite-vertex witness pattern is impossible.
At the first distinguished triangle vertex, an escaping four-point distance class cannot contain one point in each of the other two cap interiors.
At the first distinguished triangle vertex, an escaping four-point distance class cannot contain the third triangle vertex in the second cap together with one point in the third cap interior.
Cyclic relabelling excludes the five remaining versions of the three escaped witness-location patterns at the second and third distinguished triangle vertices.
Every positive-radius distance class with at least four points centered at one of the three distinguished triangle vertices is contained in the corresponding cap region.
One positive radius places every point of each endpoint cap on the circle centered at its corresponding distinguished triangle vertex.
Under cap containment and the four-equidistant-witness property, no point of the nine-point configuration lies in the interior of any endpoint cap.
